shots.action: A close view of a bus window at night, the dark glass filling the frame with rain beaded across it. Droplets sit trembling in place, then gather weight, merge and begin to crawl downward in wavering silver trails, dragging thin wakes behind them. Beyond the wet pane the city has collapsed into soft out-of-focus discs of amber, white and cold blue light that hover and drift slightly as the vehicle moves. A faint dim reflection of the dark bus interior ghosts over the glass without resolving into anything.

description.text: A close view of a bus window at night: dark glass fills the frame, beaded with rain. Small droplets tremble in place, then gather weight, merge and begin to crawl downward in wavering silver trails that drag thin wakes behind them. Some beads sit high and round, catching tiny pinpricks of light; others have already stretched into short vertical smears. Beyond the wet pane the city collapses into soft out-of-focus discs of amber, white and cold blue light, hovering and drifting slightly as the vehicle moves. A faint dim reflection of the dark bus interior ghosts over the glass without resolving into anything. The glass surface holds a thin sheen along the beads, and the dark exterior presses close beyond the scattered highlights. The wet pane dominates the frame, its droplets reading as both clear lenses and tiny shadows against the city glow.
The camera pushes in with small amplitude at slow speed.

The same rain-streaked bus window holds in view as the vehicle carries it along the street. Long smeared streaks of streetlamps, shop signs and passing headlights rake across the wet glass, sliding sideways and stretching as they go. Individual droplets break apart under the sweep of light and re-form farther along the pane, their shadows thickening and thinning. The bokeh behind them flares briefly, then fades back into the dark. A few fat drops cling near the lower edge and release in short, uneven runs, while fine mist beads in the narrow gaps between larger trails. The passing light turns the glass into a shifting map of bright lines and dark spaces, and the street outside stays soft, anonymous and continuous beyond the rain.
The camera tracks with the subject with small amplitude at slow speed.
